title: Placement Term Schedule for Placed Consumer Accounts
content:
Schedule to the client placement terms for **Placed Consumer Accounts**. It fixes, for each placement stage, how long a stage runs, the window in which a recent payment counts toward a term extension, how much one extension adds, how many extensions a stage allows, and what happens at term end when no extension applies.

| Stage | Placement term (calendar days from the stage start date) | Extension look-back window before the term end date (calendar days) | One extension adds (calendar days) | Most extensions at the stage | Term-end disposition when no extension applies |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Early-Out Placement | 150 | 30 | 60 | 1 | Return to client |
| Primary Placement | 365 | 60 | 90 | 2 | Convert to Warehouse Placement |
| Secondary Placement | 365 | 60 | 90 | 2 | Convert to Warehouse Placement |
| Tertiary Placement | 455 | 60 | 90 | 2 | Return to client |
| Warehouse Placement | 1095 | 90 | 180 | 1 | Return to client |
| Legal Review Placement | 730 | 90 | 180 | 3 | Return to client |

## Terms used in the schedule

- **Placement term**: the length of the stage, counted in calendar days from the stage start date recorded on the account.
- **Extension look-back window**: the number of calendar days ending on the term end date within which a posted payment qualifies the account for a term extension.
- **One extension adds**: the calendar days one term extension adds to the term end date.
- **Most extensions at the stage**: the largest number of term extensions an account may receive at that stage.
- **Term-end disposition**: either the account is returned to the client, or it is converted to Warehouse Placement.

## Reading the schedule

Only Primary Placement and Secondary Placement convert to Warehouse Placement at term end; the four other stages return the account to the client. Legal Review Placement allows the most extensions (3), and Early-Out Placement and Warehouse Placement allow one each.

*Hypothetical illustration:* an Early-Out Placement account whose single extension has already been granted has used the stage's whole allowance, while a Legal Review Placement account with one extension granted still has two left.
